per_key_checks.assessment: Accurate: synthetic fallback NAME for an image data URI with no usable encoded name, no extension, no placeholder. Feminine agreement with imagen is internal to the Spanish string (imagen pegada), not with any inserted text; nothing is inserted here. Parallel to the shipped sibling ui.chat.composer_media.pasted_file = "Archivo pegado" (participle after noun), and the pasted/pasted-type family in the same file ("Pegado {mimeType}") is untouched. Sentence case, no trailing punctuation, no numeral or product-name policy at stake. 13 chars vs 12 en; no maxCells hint on this key and no length budget for a fallback filename caption.

Accurate and grammatical for any inserted user string: {"name"} preserved byte-exactly, once, plain string, no ICU needed; the phrase carries no case/number/gender agreement with the inserted name, so Latin, CJK, quoted or punctuated names render unchanged (verified by formatting with "informe final (2).pdf" -> "Acciones de informe final (2).pdf"). Card position: postposed complement with de, which matches BOTH shipped generic labels of the same menu family - ui.common.actions.file_actions_menu.file_actions = "Acciones del archivo" and ui.teamBridge.actions.label = "Acciones del mensaje" - rather than the para form in ui.teamBridge.row.menu = "Más acciones para {name}" (a row menu with a different English frame). Checked the de + el contraction hazard: a name literally starting with an article would yield "de el ...", but the context note requires the name verbatim and never declined, so no re-wording can fix it and English shares the hazard.

Accurate: generic tooltip and unspecified-image accessible-name fallback for the overflow menu; the named case correctly routes to actions_for_name. Parallel to the shipped "Acciones del archivo" (File actions) and to its own siblings in the same block ("Copiar imagen", "Ampliar imagen"), with the definite article the shipped es family uses. Sentence case, no trailing punctuation, imagen is the settled word for the object. 21 chars vs 13 en, no constraint for a tooltip/accessible name.

Accurate and correctly scoped: it names playback position for one clip, not an action, and retains the clip label as the note requires (only the surrounding word for position is translated). {label} byte-exact, once, plain. Word order moves the label after de, which the note explicitly permits, and no part of the string agrees with the label, so any title - Latin, CJK, numeric, quoted - stays verbatim (verified with "Nota de voz 2026-11-10" -> "Posición de Nota de voz 2026-11-10"). Term matches the shipped ui.chat.attachments.playback_position = "Posición de reproducción"; sibling audio labels keep the auxiliary-free imperative pattern ("Reproducir {label}", "Pausar {label}"). Sentence case, no trailing punctuation.

attachment-encode.ts (HEAD): the synthetic name from getFileName() is passed as AttachmentUploadSource.name and the stored result wins (stored.name ?? name), the dataUrl source is passed untouched, and valid decoded names are returned verbatim - matching "also used as synthetic upload metadata" and "valid names and attachment bytes stay unchanged".
The sibling pasted_image note ("no usable encoded name, including invalid percent encoding") also matches the same function.
